_comment: Source of truth for Wren's App Store listing in its primary language.
Every other locale is translated from this file, so edit it here and
re-run the push rather than editing anything in App Store Connect by hand.
Apple's limits: name 30, subtitle 30, promotionalText 170, keywords 100,
description 4000. The push script checks all of them before sending.
Shared fields — name and the two URLs — come from common.json.
subtitle: Place lists into map guides
promotionalText: Share a reel or a post to Wren and it reads the places out of it, ready to check and save to Apple Maps. Screenshots and exported lists work too.
description:
Someone sends you a reel. Five places you have to eat at in Rome, a rooftop bar in Lisbon, a bookshop down an alley in Tokyo. You mean to remember. By Thursday it is gone.

Wren catches them — off a screenshot, out of a list another app exported, or from a guide you already keep — and puts them where you will be standing when you need them.

FOUR WAYS IN

Places do not only arrive as screenshots, so there are four ways to hand them over. All of them end in the same place: a guide in Apple Maps.

1. FROM A REEL OR A POST. Share it to Wren and the places are read out of it. Wren's server fetches the post, reads it and discards it — the video never reaches your phone. Paid, with 250 posts a month.

2. FROM SCREENSHOTS. One tap per place, from a reel, a post, a message from a friend, or a photographed page of a guidebook. Text recognition runs on your phone, so the screenshots stay there. Wren also reads the caption to work out which city you are looking at, and asks you to confirm it.

3. FROM A FILE. A list exported from another app — CSV, KML, KMZ, GPX, GeoJSON, or a Google Takeout export of your saved places. Where the file carries coordinates, each place is looked up near its own, so a list spanning three cities resolves correctly rather than being dragged towards one of them.

4. FROM A GUIDE YOU ALREADY HAVE. Share a guide out of Apple Maps, paste the link into Wren, and it reads the places already in it. Newly found places sit alongside them, and one guide is made holding both.

THEN YOU CHECK IT

Every place shows what was read beside what was matched, so a wrong match is obvious rather than confident. Anything not found — or found wrongly — can be searched again by hand. Nothing is written to Apple Maps until you say so.

What comes out is not a copy of your places in another app. It is an actual guide, in the Maps you already use, on every device signed in to your Apple Account. About a hundred and fifty places fit in one guide; beyond that Wren splits them into numbered guides and tells you before it does, rather than quietly dropping the ones that would not fit.

ANYWHERE, NOT JUST RESTAURANTS

Restaurants and bars, certainly. Also viewpoints, markets, hotels, galleries, shops, trailheads, beaches and the odd petrol station someone insists does the best coffee for fifty miles. Anywhere with a name and a location.

NO ACCOUNT, NO SIGN-IN

Wren has no account and reads nothing from yours. Screenshots are read on your device and are never uploaded.

Three things leave your phone, and only when you ask: the name of a place, sent to Apple Maps so it can be found, exactly as the Maps app does; a shared guide link, sent to Apple to be expanded; and the link to a reel or post you share, sent to Wren's own server, which fetches that post, reads the names out of it and discards it. Nothing about the post is kept.

FREE, WITH OPTIONAL PURCHASES

Guides of up to three places are free, for good, and so is reading a screenshot. Two one-time purchases: one removes the three-place cap and lets you add to a guide you already have, the other reads places out of a shared post. Buying both together costs less than buying them apart. No subscription, and everything restores on your other devices.

WHAT APPLE ALLOWS, PLAINLY

Apple Maps offers no way to add to an existing guide from outside the app, so combining makes a new guide holding the old places and the new ones together — Wren keeps them, so it can be made again in a tap.

reviewNotes:
WHERE THE IN-APP PURCHASE IS

From a cold start, with nothing added and no account needed:

    1. Open Wren.
    2. Tap the three-dot menu at the TOP RIGHT of the main screen.
    3. Tap "Guides of any size".

That opens the purchase sheet, showing the StoreKit price and an "Unlock for
<price>" button, plus "Restore a previous purchase". This is the only In-App
Purchase in the app: one non-consumable, "Guides of any size", product id
com.spencerfields.littlebird.unlimited.

Two further purchases exist in App Store Connect for a feature that is not in
this build. They are not submitted with this version and cannot be reached in
it.

The same sheet also appears through the features it pays for, if you would
rather reach it that way:

    * Add four or more places, then tap "Make a guide" -- the free tier saves
      three places per guide.
    * Or use "From an existing guide" (step 3 below), which is paid whatever the
      number of places.

The app is iPhone-only (TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = 1). On an iPad it runs in
iPhone compatibility mode, where the menu is in the same place.

SHARING INTO WREN

New: Wren appears in the iOS share sheet. Screenshot anything listing place
names, tap Share, choose Wren, then open Wren -- it is waiting, and the places
are read as through "Add screenshots". An Apple Maps guide link shared this way
imports the same way.

iOS does not permit a share extension to open its containing app, so it writes
what it is handed into an App Group, shows a tick and finishes. That is
deliberate. A link to a post on a social platform is declined, with a message
saying Wren reads screenshots rather than links. Wren never fetches, stores or
displays third-party media.

TESTING THE APP

Tap "Add" at the bottom left. It offers three sources:

    1. "Add screenshots" -- take or save a few screenshots containing place
       names and select them. Wren reads the names on device with the Vision
       framework, asks which city they are in, and finds them with MapKit.
       "Make a guide" then opens Maps with the places in a new guide.

    2. "From a file" -- opens the document picker and reads a list exported from
       another app: CSV, KML, KMZ, GPX, GeoJSON, or a Google Takeout export.
       Each row is looked up with MapKit, aimed at the coordinate in the file
       where there is one. A sample CSV is two lines:
           name,latitude,longitude
           Padella,51.5054,-0.0903

    3. "From an existing guide" -- paste a guide link, which Maps produces via
       Share then Copy Link. Wren decodes the places already in it and shows
       them as a collapsed group. This is the second paid feature.

On point 3: there is no way to add places to an existing guide, so publishing
produces a NEW guide holding the old places and the new ones together. The app
says so before publishing and the App Store description says so too. It is a
limit of the guide link format, not an attempt to duplicate anyone's data.

Wren requires no account and no sign-in.

IF YOU WOULD RATHER NOT TRANSACT

There is a complimentary code that unlocks both paid features without a
purchase. Please use it only after looking at the purchase sheet above, because
entering it unlocks the app and the purchase entry then disappears -- there is
nothing left to buy.

Long-press the "Wren" title at the top left of the main screen, then enter:

    7QFG-7FVY-QXP6-2AT6

This entry point is not advertised in the app. Codes are checked against a
server and cannot be shared onward. This one is not single-use and keeps
working across resubmissions.

A few codes also open a developer console for issuing codes. The one above is
not one, so it cannot be opened during review. It sells nothing and changes no
feature.

Entering a code is the only time Wren contacts a server of its own. It sends
the code and a random device identifier, nothing else. An administrator's code
re-confirms daily; the one above is not one. Everything else happens on the
device.
whatsNew:
Share a reel or a post to Wren, and it reads the places out of it.

Somebody sends you five restaurants in Rome. Share the post to Wren — no screenshots, no typing — and the names come back ready to check and save to Apple Maps. Wren's server fetches the post, reads it and discards it. The video never reaches your phone and Wren never keeps it.

Screenshots work exactly as they did, and are still free.

Reading posts is a one-time purchase with a fair-use allowance of 250 posts a month. If you already own Guides of Any Size there is a smaller price to add it.
